units.text: Recommendation: retain and optimize East through its 2029 lease end, and use 2027–28 to test the cross-dock alternative before the lease decision
Neither closure option both saves money and meets the board's 2027 constraints
Governing thought: Keep East in 2027 and optimize it (Option K: saves $0.30M a year for $0.15M one-time), and run a capped cross-dock test
Closing East saves at most $0.10M a year, not the $1.3M claimed, and fails or cannot yet prove the SLA, capacity and evidence tests
The 2029 lease end is the real decision point

Closing East does not pay once routing and handling are counted. The CFO's $1.3M is East's gross fixed cost. Serving 200k Eastern orders from Central adds $1.0M of transport (200k × $5) and $0.2M of damage: a net $0.10M a year, zero at 2028 volume, before the $0.75M exit fee
The cross-dock costs $0.15M a year more than today: $3 extra per order ($0.60M) outweighs the $0.45M fixed-cost reduction
Optimized retention (K) is the cheapest design in the base case: $8.44M in 2027, $0.20–0.45M a year below either closure
Closure also breaks, or cannot yet prove, the board's binding constraints. Close to Central: 90.3% network two-day rate vs the 92% contract
Close to Central: Central at 100% of capacity in 2027 and 108% in 2028 (at 100% from day one; even a lower-growth case does not fit)
The $1.1M retrofit close-to-Central needs is unbudgeted and would take one-time spend to $1.85M vs $0.9M authorized
Cross-dock: 93.9% on paper, but from a 6-week, non-holiday pilot with no all-ZIP definition and no promotion guarantee
Retain and optimize: 95.1% network rate, Central at 47% in 2028, $0.15M one-time
Optimize now, test the cross-dock, and decide the 2029 lease at a Q3 2028 gate. Approve Option K and a capped cross-dock test (≤$0.25M) through holiday 2027 and spring 2028, measured on all ZIP codes
Waiting avoids the $0.75M early-exit fee and settles whether the $0.85M minimum is extra or credited; that point swings the cross-dock's cost by $0.85M a year
Drop close-to-Central: its $5-per-order penalty makes it no cheaper than today at 2028 volume, even if Central were expanded
Based only on the board briefing pack (synthetic case data). All figures are in US$, at 2027 volumes unless stated
We tested four network designs and a deferral path against the board's four tests plus reversibility, using all-in cost and the contracted all-ZIP service KPI
SQ Status quo: Keep all three sites as they are today. This is the reference case
K Retain and optimize: Renegotiate East staffing shifts and add a transfer buffer for low-volume SKUs. Saves $0.30M a year for $0.15M upfront (facility audit)
C Close East, serve from Central: End the East lease in 2027 ($0.75M) and ship all 200k Eastern orders from Central at $13 each
X Close East, use a cross-dock: End the East lease and sign a two-year deal with a third-party Eastern cross-dock: $11 per order plus a $0.85M annual minimum
D Defer (middle path): Run K now, test the cross-dock through holiday peak, and decide at the 2029 lease end
Test 1 Economics: Lowest all-in annual cost: transport, facility fixed cost and damage, plus one-time cost. Not the CFO's carrier-only cost per shipment
Test 2 Service: At least 92% of all orders delivered within two days, network-wide, on all ZIP codes (the contracted KPI, not the ex-rural dashboard)
Test 3 Capacity: Central at or below its 360k certified practical capacity in 2027 and under 2028 growth (+10% East, +6% Central)
Test 4 Funding and lease: No more than $0.9M of one-time change cost in 2027; East early exit $0.75M; West lease fixed to 2030
Test 5 Risk: Decision-grade evidence and reversibility (rebuilding East-type capacity takes nine months)

Burden of proof: closing East is hard to reverse (nine months plus customer migrations) and must pass all five tests on today's evidence. Where the evidence is incomplete, we say so and treat it as a risk, not a pass
Our working hypothesis, the CEO's 'keep East open in 2027' (because Central has too little spare capacity for demand growth), held up under testing, but it needed three refinements
Condition a, Closing saves little once all costs are counted: HOLDS. Close to Central nets $0.10M a year (vs $1.3M claimed) and $0 at 2028 volume; the cross-dock costs $0.15M a year more than today
Condition b, Closing puts the 92% SLA at risk: PARTLY. Close to Central: 90.3% (fail). Cross-dock: 93.9% on paper, from non-peak pilot data
Condition c, Central cannot absorb Eastern demand: PARTLY. True for close to Central: 108% of capacity in 2028. Not relevant to the cross-dock, which does not use Central
Condition d, Keeping East fits the lease and budget: HOLDS. Lease runs to 2029 with no fee; K needs $0.15M of the $0.9M authorized
Condition e, Keeping East is the cheapest way to meet the SLA: HOLDS. Yes: even unoptimized, East ($8.74M) beats the only SLA-compliant closure option ($8.89M). K is cheaper still at $8.44M
Refined answer 1: Retain and optimize, not just retain. Option K beats the status quo by $0.30M a year at low risk
Refined answer 2: Capacity only rules out close-to-Central. The cross-dock fails on cost ($0.45M a year above K in the base case) and on unproven peak service
Refined answer 3: Keep East through 2029, not permanently. The early-exit fee falls away at lease end. Test the cross-dock now and decide at a Q3 2028 gate
Five claims in the board pre-read overstate the case for one side or the other and should not anchor the decision

“Closing East saves $1.3M a year” (CFO slide): counts East's fixed cost only. Leaves out the higher Central-to-East transport (+$5 × 200k), $0.2M extra damage and the $0.75M exit fee. Evidence-based figure: $0.10M a year before the $0.75M exit fee (–$0.65M in 2027); $0 at 2028 volume

Cost per shipment as the cost KPI (CFO dashboard): carrier invoice ÷ orders; excludes warehouse rent, returns and replacements, so it is a transport KPI only. Use all-in cost: $8.44–8.89M a year by option
“East delivers 98% in two days” (Finance report): excludes rural deliveries; the contract KPI counts every ZIP code. Evidence-based figure: 96% all-ZIP

“East causes 8 pts higher renewal” (Marketing): correlation only. East serves more high-volume accounts with dedicated sales teams, and this is not controlled for. Not usable as causal evidence; retention response to service is unknown

“Close in June 2027 and absorb at Central with today's staffing” (cost consultant): puts Central at its full 360k practical load before any demand spike; 2028 growth takes it past capacity. 100% of capacity in 2027; 108% in 2028

Implication: these corrections cut both ways. They remove most of the closure saving (CFO, consultant) and also the inflated service and loyalty case for keeping East (Finance, Marketing). The decision rests on the corrected figures

Option C arithmetic: Fixed cost removed: East site $1.30M a year. Transport: 200k orders × ($13 − $8) = $1.00M a year. Damage: +$0.20M a year for transshipped goods. Net 2027: 1.30 − 1.00 − 0.20 = $0.10M
Break-even volume (C vs status quo): $1.10M ÷ $5 = 220k Eastern orders, exactly the 2028 forecast
Option C saving waterfall, $M: East fixed cost removed 1.3; higher transport (200k × $5) 1; transshipment damage 0.2; net saving 2027 0.1; extra orders in 2028 (20k × $5) 0.1; net saving 2028 0
Not yet included, all make it worse: $0.75M exit fee: 7.5-year payback at $0.10M a year, for a lease that ends in 2029 anyway

Not yet included: carrier surcharge needed to lift Eastern service above 84% (not priced); the 84% can be lifted only with a carrier surcharge that the $13 rate does not include. Any surcharge widens C's existing $0.20M-a-year cost gap to K
Not yet included: $1.1M Central retrofit needed once 2028 growth arrives
Compared with Option K, close-to-Central is $0.20M a year more expensive even before these items
On an all-in basis, retaining and optimizing East (Option K) is the cheapest design in both 2027 and 2028 under the base reading of the cross-dock quote
One-time cost, 2027, $M: SQ 0.00; K 0.15; C 0.75; X 0.75 (systems $0.15M; exit $0.75M)
Central and West transport $2.84M in every option in 2027 (Central orders × $9 = 1.44; West 140k × $10 = 1.40); 2028 Central 1.53, West 1.40

Facility fixed cost, $M: SQ 4.30; K 4.00 (K's $0.30M audit saving shown against facility cost); C 3.00; X 3.85 (incl. 0.85 min.). East fixed $1.30M (K 1.00); Central + West fixed $1.80M + $1.20M = 3.00
Extra damage and handling: SQ –; K –; C 0.20; X in quote
Annual all-in cost above Option K, $M: 2027: SQ 0.3; C 0.2; X 0.45. 2028: SQ 0.3; C 0.3; X 0.51
So what: K is $0.45M cheaper than the status quo over 2027–28 after its $0.15M setup cost
Both closure options cost more than K every year, and the gap widens as Eastern volume grows, because each extra Eastern order costs $3–5 more to serve
C excludes the unpriced carrier surcharge and the $1.1M retrofit. 2028 assumes +10% East, +6% Central, West flat (2028 = East 220k, Central 169.6k, West 140k)
Closing East would beat optimized retention only if Eastern volume fell below 160k orders, against 200k in 2027 and 220k forecast for 2028
Saving vs K = fixed cost avoided − added cost − (rate gap × Eastern orders V). C: ($1.30M − $0.30M − $0.20M) − $5 × V → zero at V = 160k. ($0.30M = K's saving, lost if East closes)
Break-even Eastern orders: C Close to Central 160k vs K, 220k vs status quo; X Cross-dock 50k vs K, 150k vs status quo
A lower-growth case does not rescue closure: 2027 Eastern volume is already 200k. Volume would have to fall 20% (close to Central) or 75% (cross-dock) for closure to beat K
Break-even lines show the annual all-in saving vs Option K; one-time costs excluded. Assumes rates and fixed costs do not change with volume
Moving Eastern orders to Central would breach the contracted 92% two-day SLA; the cross-dock clears it on paper by 1.9 points
The threshold that matters: 88.3%, the minimum Eastern all-ZIP two-day rate that keeps the network at 92%: (460.0k − 283.4k) ÷ 200k
Close to Central (84%) is 4.3 pts short of the 88.3% threshold
The cross-dock pilot (93%) has 4.7 pts of headroom, but on non-peak data with an unstated measurement basis
Retaining East (96%) has 7.7 pts of headroom
We ignore Finance's 98% (excludes rural ZIPs) and the online dashboard measure. Neither is the contract KPI
Network-wide two-day rate margin vs the 92% contract floor, 2027, points: K / SQ Retain East (East 96%) 3.08; X Cross-dock (East 93% pilot) 1.88; C Close to Central (East 84%) -1.72
C needs 460k on-time orders but delivers 451k, so about 8,600 orders a year fall short, triggering retailer penalty clauses

Assumes Central (94%) and West (95%) keep their current two-day rates in every option (generous to C: Central at 100% load would probably slip). East's 96% is all-ZIP; the basis of the 84% (modeled) and the 93% (pilot) is not stated
The cross-dock's 93% comes from a short, non-peak pilot. It needs a holiday-peak, all-ZIP test before the board relies on it
6% of annual Eastern volume tested: 12,000 orders vs 200k a year
6 wks pilot length, no holiday weeks. Peak weeks carry the most service risk
Measurement basis '?': the quote does not say whether the 93% covers all ZIP codes
None: service guarantee for the national spring promotion. The operator has not committed to promotion volumes
Proposed gate criterion, Coverage: holiday peak 2027 and the spring 2028 promotion, including rural ZIPs
Gate criterion, Cross-dock service: at least 92% all-ZIP over the full test period and at least 90% in peak weeks
Gate criterion, Network SLA (modeled): ≥93.5%, keeping a 1.5-pt buffer
Gate criterion, Contract: SLA defined on all ZIP codes, a termination-for-cause clause (the provider will accept this), and clarity on whether the $0.85M minimum is extra or credited; budget fit
Proposed test criterion, Cost: measured damage and handling rate on transshipped goods

Eastern rate scenarios (East rate / Network / East headroom vs 88.3%): Pilot as reported 93.0% / 93.9% / +4.7 pts; If the pilot excluded rural ZIPs (–2 pts) 91.0% / 93.1% / +2.7 pts; Break-even for the 92% contract 88.3% / 92.0% / 0
The 2-pt gap mirrors East's ex-rural (98%) vs all-ZIP (96%) difference and is illustrative only. Test thresholds are proposed by Northline analysis
A full-year rate is a weighted average. If peak weeks run well below the pilot, the remaining headroom of roughly 3–5 points can disappear, and the two-year contract minimum would already be signed
Why capacity rules out Option C. 2027: 160k Central + 200k Eastern = 360k, with zero headroom for the national promotion or peaks
2028: 169.6k + 220k = 389.6k, which is 29.6k orders over capacity
Lower-growth case (half the forecast: East +5%, Central +3%) is illustrative; the pack asks for one to be discussed but does not size it. C, 2028 lower growth: 14.8k above the 360k certified capacity
Any positive growth breaches capacity; only zero growth fits, and then exactly at 100%
The fix does not fit the plan: expansion needs a two-quarter permit and a $1.1M retrofit that is not in the 2027 budget
Capacity is not a reason to reject the cross-dock or K, because neither adds load to Central (47% in 2028; K or X, 2028 forecast 169.6k)
Retention and the deferral path fit easily within the $0.9M one-time authority; close-to-Central fits only if the $1.1M Central retrofit it needs is left unfunded
One-time network change cost, $M (board authority: $0.9M): K Retain + optimize 0.15; D K + cross-dock test 0.4; X Cross-dock 0.75; C Close to Central incl. retrofit 1.85

East lease: exit in 2027 costs a one-time $0.75M; otherwise the lease expires in 2029. Waiting to 2029 avoids the early-termination fee (the $0.75M termination charge falls away; any transfer costs within it may remain); this is the natural point to decide
West lease: cannot be changed before 2030. Outside this decision; West stays as-is
Central: fixed cost unchanged in every option; any expansion needs a permit and a $1.1M retrofit. No cost saving from adding load; expansion has to be budgeted for 2028 or later
Cross-dock: two-year minimum at $0.85M a year; open to a termination-for-cause clause if the SLA is all-ZIP. Signing in 2027 locks in about $1.7M of minimums before peak service is proven

Option C's $1.85M = $0.75M East exit and transfer + $1.1M Central retrofit. Without the retrofit, C leaves only $0.15M of authority for customer migration; with it, C is over budget, and a two-quarter permit means the retrofit could not be ready for a June 2027 closure
The board's rule that service cannot be degraded to win a freight discount also limits any attempt to close C's cost gap through cheaper, slower carriers
The cross-dock test cost is capped at $0.25M with no two-year minimum: a Northline assumption, pending a provider quote (no test quote in the pack, only a two-year minimum; needs provider agreement)
Only optimized retention (K, alone or with the test in D) passes all five tests. The cross-dock fails on cost and is unproven on service; close-to-Central fails four tests
Scorecard SQ Status quo: Economics FAIL ($0.30M a year dearer than K); Service PASS (95.1%); Central capacity PASS (47% in 2028); Funding and lease PASS ($0); Risk and reversibility PASS (No change)
Scorecard K Retain + optimize: PASS on all five. Cheapest: $8.44M (2027); 95.1%, watch shift changes; 47% in 2028; $0.15M of $0.9M; Fully reversible
Scorecard D K + test, decide in 2028: PASS on all five. K's cost, ≤$0.25M buys the option; 95.1%; 47% in 2028; $0.40M of $0.9M; Generates the missing evidence

Scorecard X Close, use cross-dock: Economics FAIL (+$0.45M a year vs K, base case); Service UNPROVEN (93.9% from non-peak pilot); Central capacity PASS (Central unaffected); Funding and lease PASS ($0.75M; $0.15M spare); Risk FAIL (Two-year minimum; nine months to reverse)

Scorecard C Close, serve from Central: Economics FAIL (+$0.20M a year vs K; $0 saving vs SQ by 2028); Service FAIL (90.3%); Central capacity FAIL (100% in 2027, 108% in 2028); Funding and lease PARTLY ($0.75M fits; $1.1M retrofit unbudgeted); Risk FAIL (Nine months to reverse)
Read-across: K and D pass on today's evidence. D adds a cheap option on the cross-dock for the 2029 lease decision, so it is the recommended path
'Unproven' counts as a fail until a peak test is complete
Deferring the decision to the 2029 lease end costs little and answers the one contract question that could make the cross-dock worthwhile
Reading A (base case): $0.85M minimum is a fixed fee on top of $11 per order. Cross-dock vs K: +0.45 cost in 2027, +0.51 cost in 2028. Never worth closing East at forecast volumes

Reading B (sensitivity): $0.85M is a spend floor, credited against the $11-per-order charges. Cross-dock vs K: –0.40 saving in 2027, –0.34 saving in 2028. Could be worth it if peak all-ZIP service is proven

The cross-dock $0.85M minimum is treated as a fixed fee on top of $11 per order (Reading A); Reading B is a sensitivity, not the base case: the pack lists the $0.85M under fixed facility cost. Under Reading B the cross-dock would be $0.34–0.40M a year cheaper than K, but still unproven on service: this is why we test, not close

Why waiting beats closing now, even under Reading B. Closing in 2027 gains little: under Reading B the 2027–28 gain over K is $0.40M + $0.34M − $0.75M exit + $0.15M of K setup avoided = $0.14M over two years
The downside is lopsided: each point of Eastern service below 88.3% adds 2,000 late orders a year and pushes the network below the 92% contract floor, with penalties and nine months to reverse

What the deferral path costs and buys: K saving locked in now $0.30M a year; Test cost (capped) ≤$0.25M one-time; Early-exit fee avoided by waiting to 2029 up to $0.75M; Cross-dock minimums not committed before proof about $1.7M over two years; Decision date Q3 2028 board gate
Close-to-Central is dropped, not deferred: it loses to K at any volume above 160k
Execute in three steps: optimize East now, test the cross-dock through peak and promotion, and take the 2029 lease decision at a Q3 2028 gate
Step 1, Q1–Q2 2027, Optimize East (Option K): Approve $0.15M for systems changes. Renegotiate East staffing shifts; set up the low-volume SKU transfer buffer
Guardrail: East all-ZIP two-day rate at or above 95%, tracked weekly
Confirm East can handle 220k orders in 2028
Step 2, Q2 2027 – Q2 2028, Test the cross-dock: Negotiate a test contract: all-ZIP SLA, termination for cause, how the minimum is treated
Route a sample of Eastern orders, including rural ZIPs, through holiday 2027 and spring 2028. Measure the all-ZIP rate, peak weeks, damage and cost per order
Step 3, Q3 2028 board gate (2029 lease): Close East at lease end only if all four gate criteria are met. Otherwise renew East and keep optimizing
Either way, transition before the 2029 expiry
Decision 1: Keep East open in 2027; do not serve the East region from Central
Decision 2: Approve Option K ($0.15M one-time)
Decision 3: Authorize a cross-dock test of up to $0.25M with an all-ZIP SLA and no two-year minimum (subject to provider agreement)
Decision 4: Schedule the 2029 lease gate for Q3 2028
Gate criterion, Cross-dock cost: at least $0.2M a year below K at forecast volume

Gate timing Q3 2028, before the 2029 lease expiry: timing assumes the 2029 lease expiry leaves at least six months after the gate; expiry month not given; confirm the exact expiry date. The gate thresholds are proposals
The recommendation holds under the main uncertainties. Each one has a monitoring trigger and a planned response

K's $0.30M saving does not materialize (audit estimate). Still the right call: the status quo ($8.74M) beats the cross-dock ($8.89M), and close-to-Central fails the SLA and capacity tests regardless. Track savings quarterly; stop the shift changes if service suffers
Shift renegotiation hurts East service. Headroom is 7.7 pts on the Eastern rate (96% vs 88.3%). Weekly all-ZIP tracking; act if East drops below 95%

Growth falls short (marketplace promotion not contracted). Closure still loses: 2027 volume is already 200k, above every break-even except C vs status quo (220k). Rerun break-evens at the Q3 2028 gate with actual volumes
Growth beats forecast. East site capacity is not stated in the pack; 220k is assumed to fit. Confirm East capacity in the Q1 2027 audit

Customer retention response to service is unknown. Not used: the 92% contract floor binds regardless; Marketing's 8-pt claim is confounded. Run a controlled renewal analysis (by account size and sales coverage)
Cross-dock peak performance, damage rate and contract terms are unknown. These are exactly what the test resolves; no commitment before the gate. Gate criteria on slide 15
Central permit timing is unknown. Matters only for close-to-Central, which is dropped. None needed now
Memo: X under Reading B (minimum credited against charges): all-in annual cost 8.04 in 2027, 8.35 in 2028

Not modeled because the pack gives no figure: the carrier surcharge for C, the $1.1M retrofit (timing), returns and replacements, customer penalties, and any change in Central's 94% service under full load. Totals may not add due to rounding
Where K's $0.30M lands: reduction of East facility and operating cost. Placement does not affect totals
Damage under C in 2028: held at $0.20M (not scaled to volume). Scaling would make C worse by $0.02M
Analyst choices were made without client input because the pack is silent or ambiguous; each is stated so the board can challenge it; none changes the recommendation except where noted
